bibl.title: Indian trade between the Gulf and the Red Sea.
bibl.seg: Michał Gawlikowski, Indian trade between the Gulf and the Red Sea.
Iwona Zych (ed.), Polish Archaeology in the Mediterranean. 26/2. Research on the Red Sea (Warsaw, 2017) pp. 15-30, figg.
bibl.note: Evaluates the relative importance of the maritime trade between the Roman Empire and India along two routes that were in use: one started and ended on the Egyptian coast of the Red Sea, the other at the head of the Gulf. Both continued on land, following the caravan tracks to the Nile valley or through the Syrian desert to Palmyra. An inscription from Palmyra allows the value of the trade along the Syrian route to be estimated as much smaller than that of the Red Sea traffic.
